blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Fraud checks are lambdas of one functional interface, held in a list, and every merchant sets its own amount threshold for the large-order check. The incident log names the check that rejected an order as FraudChecks$$Lambda/0x00007f3a1c00a218@6d06d69c. Which change makes the log say which check it was, with the right threshold for each merchant?

options.text: Turn each check into an enum constant that keeps its threshold in a field, since a constant prints its own name.
options.says: An enum constant is one object for the whole JVM, so one threshold field is shared by every merchant; a constant can't take parameters per use.

options.text: Turn each check into a record that implements the interface, since each instance prints its own type and threshold.
options.says: A record or class carries per-use parameters as constructor arguments and has a toString() of its own, unlike a lambda.

options.text: Assign each lambda to a static final field with a descriptive name, since the field name becomes what the lambda prints.
options.says: A lambda's toString() is a generated class name; the variable it is assigned to plays no part.

options.text: Mark the interface @FunctionalInterface, since the compiler then names each lambda's class after the interface.
options.says: The annotation only checks that the interface has one abstract method; the lambda's class name is still generated.

origin.section: A Lambda Strategy Has No Name; an Enum Strategy Has One, and One Instance per JVM

questions.stem: A money formatter is a strategy object that keeps a StringBuilder field, reused on every call to save allocations. One instance formats amounts for 40 request threads, and now and then an invoice shows digits that belong to another invoice. Which change fixes it?

options.text: Keep the field and declare it volatile, since each thread then works on the latest contents of the builder.
options.says: volatile makes each write visible to the other threads, which is the damage here; in the page's run it made wrong results far more frequent.

options.text: Keep the field and clear it with setLength(0) at the start of each call, since each call then starts from an empty builder.
options.says: Resetting shared state at the start of a call is the race itself: another thread clears it while one is halfway through.

options.text: Move the builder into a local variable of the method, since each call then has a builder no other thread can reach.
options.says: A strategy that needs nothing between calls keeps nothing: per-call values in locals or a value the call owns.

options.text: Move the formatter into an enum constant of its own, since each use of the constant then gets a fresh instance.
options.says: An enum constant is one instance for the whole JVM, so its field is shared by every thread exactly as before.

origin.section: A Strategy Object Is Shared, So a Field in It Is Shared State

questions.stem: A nightly report sorts the day's jobs with the comparator (a, b) -> (int) (a.deadlineNanos() - b.deadlineNanos()). The unit tests use jobs due a few hundred milliseconds apart. In production the deadlines are spread over several minutes. What does the report do?

options.text: It lists the jobs in deadline order every night, since the cast to int keeps the sign of the difference between two deadlines.
options.says: A difference over about 2.1 s in nanoseconds doesn't fit an int, and the cast can wrap it to the opposite sign.

options.text: It fails every night with IllegalArgumentException, since List.sort checks each comparison against the comparator's general contract.
options.says: List.sort never checks the comparator; it throws only when its merge step runs into a contradiction, and on other inputs returns a wrong order without a word.

options.text: It lists the jobs out of order or fails, depending on the order the jobs arrive in, since the sort acts on answers that contradict each other.
options.says: With wrapped differences the comparator says a < b, b < c and c < a; the sort returns a scrambled list or throws, depending on input order.

options.text: It lists the jobs in deadline order or fails, depending on the order the jobs arrive in, since the sort notices an overflowing comparator on some inputs.
options.says: When the sort doesn't throw it doesn't fix anything: in the page's run four of five inputs came back scrambled without an exception.

origin.section: The JDK's Comparator Is a Strategy, and the Sort Trusts Its Contract

questions.stem: A storage service keeps its compression codecs in a Map<String, Codec> and reads storage.compression from config. A release sets storage.compression=zstd, and this build has only gzip and none. How should the service treat the name?

options.text: Look the codec up when each file is written, since a wrong name then fails on the first write, where it is easy to see.
options.says: A lookup at first use lets the service pass its health check and deploy; the failure comes later, at a write, without naming the setting.

options.text: Look the codec up when each file is written and fall back to none, since files keep being written while the config is fixed.
options.says: A fallback for a wrong value never fails, so the service runs with a codec nobody chose until someone notices.

options.text: Look the codec up in the constructor and throw when it is missing, since the deploy then stops before any file is written.
options.says: Resolving the name at start-up makes a wrong name stop the deploy, with a message that can name the value and the choices.

options.text: Look the codec up in the constructor and fall back to gzip when it is missing, since a check at start-up and a default cover both cases.
options.says: A default belongs to a key that is absent, never to a value that is wrong; this one never fails at all.

origin.section: Resolve a Strategy's Name When the Service Starts, Not When It First Runs

concepts: An enum strategy is closed to other modules, can't take parameters per use, and each constant is one object for the whole JVM, so a policy with settings is a record, a class or a capturing lambda.

A lambda strategy's toString() is a generated class name, so logs can't say which strategy ran, and mapping a config string to a lambda needs a table you write; an enum constant prints its name and valueOf reads it from config.
